column1: # DozerDB metric inventory: every metric of the Neo4j Operations Manual 2026.10 metrics reference with its
# compatibility classification. It is the single source of truth for the
# conformance test and for the generated public compatibility matrix; the reader is MetricInventory.
# Tab-separated, UTF-8. Lines starting with # are comments; the first other line is the header; columns are
# looked up by name, so a column may be added without touching existing readers. Rows are in the reference
# page's order, grouped by its sections. No cell contains a tab; empty cells are allowed only in reason and notes.
# section            the reference page's section (its table caption; "Discovery metrics" uses the heading)
# name_template      the name as the manual writes it: <prefix>.<...>, with <db> for a database name and the
#                    instance placeholders <pool>, <gc>, <bufferpool>, resolved by the running JVM. The manual
#                    writes the scope segment (dbms. or database.<db>.) into some tables and omits it from
#                    others; the full name is always <prefix>.dbms.<metric> or <prefix>.database.<db>.<metric>.
# type               gauge | counter | histogram | timer (the manual's marker; timer for its "(counter, histogram)"
#                    rows described as a Metrics Timer)
# unit               the documented unit, or - when the manual states none
# scope_inferred     true when the manual does not state the scope and it was inferred
# lifecycle          the manual's label (Introduced in ..., Deprecated in ..., Renamed in ..., unsupported feature)
# tier               Compatible | Partial | Unsupported | Not applicable; Compatible only when a test provokes the
#                    documented event and observes the change
# reason             why the tier is not Compatible; empty for a Compatible row and required otherwise. Published
#                    verbatim in the public compatibility matrix and differences page (scripts/metrics-docs.py):
#                    written for users, about the product only
# format_provenance  the strongest source that established the output format, in the order of the compatibility
#                    oracle (step 1 the pinned manual, 2 Neo4j's Community source, 3 historical open source, 4
#                    pending for an Unsupported row (replaced once a collector emits it) and never-emitted
# docs_anchor        the row's section on the pinned reference page
# deprecated         true when the manual deprecates the metric (DozerDB still emits deprecated metrics)
# type_rule          documented (the manual's type marker was unambiguous) | oracle (the manual was ambiguous
#                    and the oracle order settled it; the notes say how)
# notes              free text for maintainers, never published in the documentation: how the scope was decided,
#                    default-filter entries, :sysinfo readers, naming questions, page errata, the tests
# CSV file names: <full metric name>.csv, prefix included (neo4j.dbms.vm.heap.used.csv). The
#                    stem is the registered name, as the 3.4 module and Dropwizard's CsvReporter both wrote it:
#                    provenance historical-open-source, to be confirmed by an Enterprise capture.
# Graphite paths: the full metric name as registered, prefix once (neo4j.dbms.vm.heap.used);
#                    a counter, histogram or timer adds Dropwizard's attribute segments (.count, .p99, .m1_rate).
#                    Paths: provenance documented; attribute segments: library-convention, corroborated by the
#                    3.4 module (historical-open-source); to be confirmed by an Enterprise capture.
# Prometheus channel: the full name with every character outside [A-Za-z0-9:] replaced by _,
#                    no added prefix, no labels; a gauge row is a gauge family; a counter row is a counter family
#                    whose sample is <name>_total; a histogram row is a summary with the quantiles 0.5, 0.75, 0.95,
#                    0.98, 0.99, 0.999 and _count, no _sum. Provenance of that mapping: dashboards (Grafana.com
#                    10371 and 12046) corroborated by third-party captures of Neo4j 4.4.0 and 5.11.0 output;
#                    an Enterprise 2026.10 capture would confirm it.
# A collector that starts emitting a metric changes its row's tier, reason, format_provenance and notes; nothing

scope: explicit .dbms. in name; default filter *bolt.connections*; emitted by BoltCollector as a counter incremented on BoltConnectionMetricsMonitor.connectionOpened (fired by MetricsConnectorListener.onProtocolSelected, so a connection counts once its protocol version is negotiated); BoltMetricsIT (a driver connection)

scope: explicit .dbms. in name; essential page workload metric; description cites dbms.connector.bolt.thread_pool_max_size, a removed setting (current key server.bolt.thread_pool_max_size); emitted by BoltCollector as a gauge kept from the events: connectionActivated minus connectionWaiting (BoltConnectionMetricsMonitor exposes no registry count), so a connection is running while a Bolt worker thread is bound to it, which with the default transaction thread binding includes the whole of an open explicit transaction; BoltMetricsIT (open transaction)

scope: explicit .dbms. in name; emitted by BoltCollector as a counter incremented on BoltConnectionMetricsMonitor.messageProcessingCompleted, which fires for every started message, failed ones included; a query answered with FAILURE is done, not failed; BoltMetricsIT

scope: explicit .dbms. in name; emitted by BoltCollector as a counter incremented on BoltConnectionMetricsMonitor.messageProcessingFailed, which fires only when processing throws out of the state machine (a fatal or connection-terminating error such as a rejected LOGON or an illegal transition), not for a query answered with FAILURE; BoltMetricsIT (authentication failure on a server with auth enabled)

scope: page text: all JVM-related metrics are global; <pool> here is the MemoryPoolMXBean name lower-cased with spaces as underscores (page example g1_survivor_space; default filter *vm.memory.pool.g1_eden_space, *vm.memory.pool.g1_old_gen), a different meaning from <pool> in the neo4j pools tables; collector JvmMemoryPoolsCollector (MemoryPoolMXBean.getUsage().getUsed(), valid pools only); <pool> rule as for <gc> (JvmInstanceNames): JDK 21 G1 yields g1_eden_space, g1_old_gen, g1_survivor_space, metaspace, compressed_class_space, codeheap_non_nmethods, codeheap_profiled_nmethods, codeheap_non_profiled_nmethods; the quoted CodeHeap spellings are unverified against Enterprise

scope: page text: all JVM-related metrics are global; page states no unit; collector JvmPauseTimeCollector: an event counter fed the milliseconds of each pauseDetected on the global Monitors bus (VmPauseMonitorAdapter); Neo4j's pause monitor measures every internal.vm_pause_monitor.measurement_duration and reports a pause once a tick overshoots by internal.vm_pause_monitor.stall_alert_threshold (200 ms each by default), so the unit is milliseconds although the page states none; default filter *vm.pause_time

scope: page text: all JVM-related metrics are global; the page's global example cites vm.thread.count, a typo for this metric; default filter *vm.thread*; collector JvmThreadsCollector (ThreadMXBean.getThreadCount: live platform threads, daemon and non-daemon)

column9: Java 21 exposes no count of live virtual threads: ThreadMXBean counts platform threads only and jdk.management.VirtualThreadSchedulerMXBean arrives in JDK 24 and counts mounted threads; Enterprise's source is unavailable
column14: scope: page text: all JVM-related metrics are global; default filter *vm.thread*; collector JvmThreadsCollector registers vm.threads only; revisit when the release line's JDK offers a live virtual thread count
